questions.stem: An investigator adds 2,4-dinitrophenol (DNP), a proton carrier that crosses the inner mitochondrial membrane, to isolated mitochondria supplied with pyruvate and oxygen. Oxygen consumption rises but ATP synthesis falls to near zero. Which best explains both observations?
options: DNP blocks the electron transport chain, so protons are no longer pumped and the gradient collapses
DNP inhibits ATP synthase directly, so the gradient builds until it back-pressures the chain
DNP dissipates the proton gradient, so electron transport runs faster without back-pressure while the synthase has no gradient to spend
DNP uncouples substrate-level phosphorylation in the matrix, which is why oxygen use increases
questions.why: The gradient is the coupling link: collapse it and electron transport accelerates (more O2 consumed) while ATP synthase has no proton-motive force to use. Direct inhibition of the chain or the synthase would slow oxygen use, not raise it.

questions.stem: A student's draft opens: "School start times are a problem. Many students are tired. Something must be done." The teacher asks for a thesis a skeptical school board could actually debate. Which revision best meets that request?
options: Later start times for the high school are worth their busing cost because adolescent sleep research, attendance data, and the district's own budget figures all favor the shift.
School start times are a serious issue that affects students, families, and the entire community in many important ways.
Everyone knows that teenagers need more sleep, so the district should simply do the right thing.
This essay will discuss the pros and cons of later start times before reaching a conclusion.
questions.why: A debatable thesis names a claim, the reason for it, and the evidence that will carry it. B is vague, C assumes the conclusion, and D announces a topic instead of asserting anything.

questions.stem: Reaction rate is measured at increasing substrate concentration. Adding a fixed amount of inhibitor X lowers Vmax but leaves Km unchanged. Adding inhibitor Y raises apparent Km but leaves Vmax unchanged. Which pair of mechanisms best fits X and Y?
options: X is competitive, because it occupies the active site; Y is noncompetitive, because it binds elsewhere
X is irreversible, because Vmax falls; Y is allosteric activation, because Km rises
Both are competitive inhibitors and differ only in how tightly they bind the active site
X binds a site other than the active site and removes enzyme from service; Y competes with substrate for the active site
questions.why: A competitive inhibitor is outrun by substrate, so Vmax holds while apparent Km rises. A noncompetitive inhibitor lowers Vmax, and the enzyme that remains active keeps its normal Km. A has the assignment backwards.

questions.stem: A student writes: "Later start times raise attendance (Alvarez 12). Students do better when they are not exhausted." The teacher marks the second sentence as commentary that does not yet earn the evidence. Which revision best connects the source to the claim?
options: Alvarez reports a 4 percent attendance gain, which matters because attendance is itself a graded outcome in most districts.
Alvarez's 4 percent gain shows the mechanism at work: rested students attend, and attendance is the first measurable step toward the credit accumulation the district tracks.
Alvarez is a professor at a state university, so the 4 percent figure should be trusted.
Attendance is important, and 4 percent is a large number for any school to gain in a single year.
questions.why: Commentary must state how the evidence supports the claim, not restate it or vouch for the source. B ties the figure to the causal chain the argument depends on; C argues credibility and D only asserts magnitude.

questions.stem: A hormone binds a G protein-coupled receptor on a liver cell, and glycogen breakdown begins within seconds. The response stops when a phosphatase is added. Which best explains both the amplification and the shutoff?
options: The hormone enters the cell and activates glycogen phosphorylase directly, and the phosphatase destroys the hormone
Receptor binding activates a G protein that turns on adenylyl cyclase; cAMP activates protein kinase A, which phosphorylates and activates enzymes, and phosphatases reverse those phosphorylations
The G protein phosphorylates glycogen directly, and the phosphatase removes phosphates from the receptor only
cAMP is the second messenger, but it prolongs the signal by binding the receptor's extracellular domain
questions.why: A peptide hormone cannot cross the membrane, so the signal is relayed and amplified by a cascade of kinases. Phosphatases erase the phosphate marks, which is why the response ends when enzyme activity, not the hormone, is reversed.

questions.stem: An essay arguing for later start times has four body paragraphs: (1) a parent's complaint about 5 a.m. bus rides, (2) sleep-lab findings on adolescent circadian shifts, (3) attendance and grade data from districts that made the shift, (4) the busing-cost objection and its rebuttal. Which reorganization best strengthens the reasoning?
options: Move the parent's complaint to the end so the essay closes on a human note.
Put the objection first so the essay can dismiss it before presenting any evidence.
Open with the sleep science, build through the outcome data, then concede and answer the cost objection, and close with the parent's account as illustration.
Alternate between the objection and the evidence paragraph by paragraph so the reader never forgets the cost.
questions.why: Reasoning moves from mechanism to outcome to the strongest objection answered. Narrative belongs as illustration, not as a premise, and a rebuttal offered before any evidence concedes ground it has not earned.

questions.stem: A single meiosis in a diploid organism yields four gametes: two carry an extra chromosome and two are missing one. Crossing over occurred normally. Which event best explains this outcome?
options: Nondisjunction of one homologous pair at meiosis I, so both homologs went to the same pole
Nondisjunction of sister chromatids at meiosis II in one cell, which would make two abnormal and two normal gametes
Failure of cytokinesis after telophase II, which yields one cell with four nuclei
Premature separation of sister chromatids at anaphase I, which cannot change chromosome number
questions.why: Meiosis I separates homologs. If a pair fails to separate, both products of that division get the extra chromosome and both products of the other division are short one, giving two n+1 and two n-1 gametes.

questions.stem: Passage: "The district's new efficiency plan arrives with a glossy cover, a consultant's timeline, and a promise that no one will notice the difference. Perhaps no one will." The final sentence mainly signals
options: enthusiastic agreement with the plan's projected savings
neutral uncertainty about whether the plan can be implemented on schedule
a factual prediction that the plan will produce no measurable change
dry skepticism that turns the plan's own promise against it
questions.why: Repeating the plan's own words as a flat prediction carries the irony: the writer expects the changes to go unnoticed because they are cosmetic. Tone here is achieved by understatement, not by stated doubt.

questions.stem: In a plant, tall (A) is dominant to dwarf (a) and round seed (B) is dominant to wrinkled (b). A tall, round plant of unknown genotype is testcrossed and produces 40 tall-round, 38 tall-wrinkled, and no dwarf offspring of either seed type. Which genotype and arrangement best fits?
options: AaBb with the genes on separate chromosomes, since both traits appear in the progeny
AABb, so only the seed-shape gene segregates and every offspring is tall
AaBB, so only height segregates and every offspring is round
AaBb with the two genes completely linked, since no recombinant types appear
questions.why: The absence of any dwarf offspring means the plant carries no a allele, so it must be AA. The 1:1 round-to-wrinkled split is the testcross signature of Bb; complete linkage in a heterozygote would still yield dwarf progeny.

questions.stem: Passage: "The board did not cut the arts program; it rebalanced instructional minutes." The quotation marks around "rebalanced" mainly
options: distance the writer from the district's word, implying the cut was renamed rather than avoided
indicate that the phrase is a direct quotation from a named board member
signal that the writer endorses the district's accounting language
mark the phrase as a technical term the reader may not know
questions.why: Scare quotes attribute a word to someone else while refusing to adopt it. The semicolon construction invites the reader to see the euphemism as a substitution for the plain word cut.

questions.stem: In a population of 1,000 beetles at Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, 90 show the recessive phenotype. Roughly how many are heterozygous, and which assumption is likeliest to fail first if the population becomes small and isolated?
options: About 210 heterozygous; mutation rate is the assumption most likely to fail
About 580 heterozygous; natural selection, because recessive phenotypes are removed
About 420 heterozygous; genetic drift, because small population size makes allele frequencies fluctuate by chance
About 420 heterozygous; random mating, because small populations mate assortatively by size
questions.why: q squared is 0.09, so q is 0.3 and p is 0.7; 2pq is 0.42, or roughly 420 individuals. The assumption that breaks first in a small isolated population is no drift, since chance sampling error grows as population size falls.

questions.stem: Passage: "The bond package funded a new scoreboard with a replay screen. Two miles away, the middle school's science labs still share one working fume hood." The juxtaposition mainly works to
options: show that the district spends money carelessly in every department
compare two facilities on a neutral list of capital projects
concede that athletic spending has some academic benefits
let the contrast imply a misplaced priority without the writer having to assert it
questions.why: The parallel construction asks the reader to draw the comparison. The writer never states that priorities are wrong, which is what makes the implication harder to argue with than an explicit charge.

questions.stem: Three species form a clade, with a fourth unrelated taxon as outgroup. Species 1 and 2 share a derived trait that species 3 lacks. Species 1 also has a trait found only in the outgroup. Which interpretation best fits?
options: Species 1 branches off first, because its unique trait makes it the most primitive member
Species 1 and 2 are sister taxa, and the trait shared with the outgroup is ancestral or convergent, since shared derived traits define clades
All three are equally related, because each carries at least one distinctive trait
Species 3 is the outgroup, so species 1 and 2 are more closely related to each other than to 3
questions.why: Only shared derived characters group taxa. A trait shared with an outgroup is ancestral at this level and cannot place species 1 outside the clade; a trait unique to one species is an autapomorphy, not evidence of early branching.

questions.stem: Passage: "The district asked for patience in September and delivered a plan in June; it asked for trust in June and has delivered nothing since." The antithesis mainly
options: pairs matched clauses so the broken promise is felt before it is named
defines patience and trust as synonyms the district prefers
softens the accusation by balancing criticism with praise
introduces statistical evidence about the plan's delay
questions.why: Balanced clauses set up an expectation of symmetry and then break it in the second half. The structure carries the charge, so the writer never has to say the district broke its word.

questions.stem: A plant cell has solute potential of -0.8 MPa and pressure potential of +0.3 MPa. It is placed in an open solution with water potential of -0.6 MPa. Which best predicts water movement and the cell's eventual state?
options: Water enters the cell, because the positive pressure potential pushes water inward
No net movement occurs, because the two water potentials are equal once pressure is counted
Water enters, because -0.6 MPa is a higher water potential than -0.5 MPa
Water leaves the cell, because the cell's water potential is higher than the solution's, and turgor pressure falls
questions.why: The cell's water potential is -0.8 plus 0.3, or -0.5 MPa, which is higher than the -0.6 MPa outside. Water moves toward lower water potential, so the cell loses water and its pressure potential declines toward plasmolysis.

questions.stem: Passage: "The gym floor held the taped line from graduation rehearsal, the folded bleachers, the smell of floor wax, and a clock still set to the last bell." Compared with "The gym was empty," this sentence mainly
options: delays the main idea until the final clause to create suspense about the closure
lists details to prove that the gym is still in use
accumulates concrete details before any interpretation, letting the reader feel the absence
uses abstract nouns to argue that the closure was mismanaged
questions.why: The sentence stacks physical particulars and never states the conclusion. The reader supplies it, which is why the effect is elegiac rather than argued; the details are concrete, not abstract.

questions.stem: A C4 grass and a C3 grass grow side by side in hot, dry, bright conditions. The C4 plant fixes carbon faster and loses less water per carbon fixed. Which best explains the advantage?
options: PEP carboxylase in mesophyll cells fixes CO2 into a four-carbon acid that concentrates CO2 around rubisco in bundle-sheath cells, suppressing photorespiration
C4 plants keep stomata open longer, so more CO2 enters and more water is retained
C4 plants use cyclic electron flow to avoid producing oxygen, so rubisco never binds O2
C4 plants run the Calvin cycle in mesophyll cells and the light reactions in bundle-sheath cells
questions.why: Spatial separation is the mechanism: PEP carboxylase has no affinity for oxygen, and the concentrated CO2 in the bundle sheath keeps rubisco oxygenase activity low. Longer stomatal opening would lose more water, not less.

questions.stem: Passage: "The memo explains that the district will invest in its people by eliminating twelve positions, and that remaining staff will benefit from the efficiencies of a leaner team." The satire works mainly by
options: attacking laid-off employees for resisting efficiency
adopting the memo's own language so its euphemisms condemn themselves
presenting budget statistics that contradict the memo's claims
proposing a specific alternative staffing plan
questions.why: Satire by borrowing lets the target's diction do the damage. The writer offers no statistics and no plan; the reader hears the mismatch between invest and eliminate and draws the indictment.

questions.stem: Ouabain blocks the sodium-potassium ATPase. In a treated neuron, the resting membrane potential slowly depolarizes toward zero. Which best explains the change?
options: The pump normally carries sodium inward, so blocking it removes an inward current and hyperpolarizes the cell
The pump generates the action potential, so blocking it prevents spikes but leaves the resting potential unchanged
With the pump blocked, sodium leak in and potassium leak out are no longer opposed, so the gradients that set the resting potential run down
Ouabain opens potassium channels directly, letting potassium enter and depolarize the cell
questions.why: The pump does not fire action potentials; it maintains the gradients. Blocked, it cannot offset passive leaks, so intracellular sodium rises and potassium falls, and the diffusion potentials that hold the membrane negative decay.

questions.stem: An op-ed replies to a proposal for later start times: "Critics want teenagers to sleep until noon and skip first period entirely." The reply is flawed because it
options: cites no expert opinion in support of its claim
uses a statistic without naming its source
concedes too much to the proposal's supporters
substitutes an extreme version of the proposal for the proposal itself
questions.why: The argument defeats a position nobody holds. Attacking the strongest version of the opposing claim would be fair; substituting a caricature is a straw man regardless of how the reply is sourced.

questions.stem: A muscle cell and a yeast cell both run glycolysis faster under anaerobic conditions, but the muscle accumulates lactate while the yeast accumulates ethanol and carbon dioxide. Which best explains why both ferment?
options: Fermentation yields more ATP per glucose than the electron transport chain does
Both cells ferment to dispose of pyruvate, which is toxic at high concentration
Fermentation keeps the Krebs cycle running by shuttling pyruvate into the mitochondria
Fermentation regenerates NAD+ from NADH, so glycolysis can keep making ATP when the chain has no oxygen to accept electrons
questions.why: Only the regeneration of NAD+ matters: without it, glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase stalls and glycolysis stops. The end product differs by organism because each uses a different electron acceptor for pyruvate.

questions.stem: Passage: "The district installed the new scoreboard in August. By October, math scores had risen. The investment in school spirit is clearly paying off in the classroom." The reasoning is flawed because it
options: assumes the scoreboard was installed before August
relies on a sample of students that is never described
treats a sequence in time as if it established a cause
attacks the district's motives instead of its evidence
questions.why: Two events in order do not show that one produced the other; a third variable such as a new curriculum could explain the rise. This is post hoc ergo propter hoc, an error about causation rather than sampling.

questions.stem: During the absolute refractory period, a second stimulus of any strength fails to trigger another action potential. Which mechanism best explains this?
options: Voltage-gated sodium channels are inactivated, so no new inward sodium current can be generated until they reset
Potassium channels are closed, so the membrane cannot repolarize
The sodium-potassium pump is saturated and cannot restore the gradient quickly enough
The threshold has fallen so low that the neuron is already firing continuously
questions.why: The inactivation gate, not the channel's closed state, is what makes the period absolute: no stimulus can reopen an inactivated channel, so the spike cannot be re-initiated until repolarization resets the gates.

questions.stem: Passage: "I asked three seniors about the new schedule, and all three said they were less stressed. The change has clearly worked for the whole school." The claim's main weakness is that it
options: uses an emotional appeal instead of any evidence
generalizes from three students to an entire school
fails to define what stress means in this context
contradicts itself about which schedule changed
questions.why: The sample is three people, self-selected and from one grade, so it cannot support a claim about the whole school. The passage does offer evidence; the problem is its scope, not its absence.

questions.stem: After a carbohydrate-heavy meal, blood glucose rises, insulin is secreted, and glucose uptake by liver and muscle increases. Hours later blood glucose falls and glucagon is secreted. Which best explains the pair of responses?
options: Insulin and glucagon are antagonistic hormones released in response to the same stimulus
Insulin raises blood glucose while glucagon lowers it, and both are released by the pancreas
Insulin lowers blood glucose and glucagon raises it, each secreted in response to the direction of the deviation
Both hormones come from the adrenal cortex and act through the same receptor
questions.why: This is negative feedback with opposing effectors: each hormone is triggered by the deviation it corrects, so the pair brackets glucose around a set point. Calling them antagonistic is only right if the response to each stimulus is stated.

questions.stem: A student's editorial on later start times, written for the school paper, opens with a joke about third period and cites a classmate's survey. The same argument must now go to the school board. Which revision best fits the new audience?
options: Keep the joke but add more classmates' quotes to show broad support
Remove all evidence and rely on the board's sense of fairness
Shorten the piece by cutting the survey, since boards prefer brevity
Replace the joke and the survey with district attendance data and the busing cost, and address the board's budget authority
questions.why: Audience shapes evidence and tone. A board answers to budgets and district data and does not share the students' inside references, so the appeal must be rebuilt on grounds that audience is accountable for.

questions.stem: Water rises in a tall oak although root pressure alone cannot lift it that far. Which combination of properties best explains the ascent?
options: Active transport of water by xylem parenchyma pushes water upward from the roots
Transpiration at the leaves pulls on a continuous water column whose cohesion and adhesion to xylem walls hold it under tension
Pressure flow in the phloem drags water upward along with sugars
Capillary action alone in the narrowest vessels is sufficient to reach the canopy
questions.why: Transpiration creates negative pressure at the top, and hydrogen bonding keeps the column from breaking while adhesion to the walls limits it from pulling away. Water is not actively pumped, and capillarity alone cannot span a tall trunk.

questions.stem: An essay arguing for later start times has already answered the busing-cost objection. Which closing move best strengthens the argument rather than merely restating it?
options: Return to the opening image of the 5 a.m. bus stop and state what the district's choice now means for the student standing there
Repeat the thesis in the same words so the reader cannot miss it
Introduce a new objection about teacher contracts that the essay never addresses
End with a dictionary definition of adolescence to broaden the scope
questions.why: A conclusion earns its place by extending the argument's stakes through the opening image rather than repeating the claim. A new unaddressed objection would weaken the piece, and a dictionary definition adds no reasoning.

questions.stem: A protein loses function when heated to 70 C but regains it when cooled slowly. A second protein treated the same way never regains function. Which best explains the difference?
options: The first protein's peptide bonds broke and then re-formed; the second's were destroyed
Both were denatured, but only the first contained disulfide bonds
Heating adds phosphate groups that inactivate proteins until a phosphatase removes them
The first protein's tertiary structure unfolded and refolded because its primary sequence stayed intact; the second's native fold was not recoverable
questions.why: Denaturation disrupts interactions that hold the folded shape, not the peptide backbone, and the sequence itself directs refolding. Irreversible loss means aggregation or covalent change has destroyed the path back to the native fold.

questions.stem: A writer has three sources on later start times: one reports a 4 percent attendance gain, one reports a 0.2 point GPA gain, and one reports that 78 percent of parents favor the change. The claim is that the shift improves academic outcomes. Which use of the data is strongest?
options: Cite the 78 percent parent figure first, because it shows the change is popular
List all three figures without comment so the reader can judge their weight
Lead with the attendance and GPA figures, then note that parent support matters for sustaining the change
Round all three to one number so the evidence looks consistent
questions.why: Evidence should be ranked by its bearing on the claim. Attendance and GPA are outcome measures, while parent opinion speaks to durability and legitimacy; leading with popularity would substitute support for outcome.

questions.stem: A forensic sample holds very little DNA. PCR with primers flanking a short locus yields millions of copies, but a second sample with a mutation in one primer-binding site yields no product. Which best explains the failure?
options: The primers cannot anneal to the mutated template, so no polymerase can extend from that site
The mutated template is too long for the polymerase to copy in the time allowed
The mutation raises the melting temperature of the whole double helix beyond what the thermocycler reaches
Primers are consumed in the first cycle, so any mutation elsewhere in the template would also block amplification
questions.why: Amplification requires both primers to base-pair at their sites; a mismatch at a binding site prevents annealing, so extension cannot start. The primer does not need to match the whole template, and a mutation elsewhere would not stop the reaction.

questions.stem: Source A finds a 4 percent attendance gain after a later start; Source B, a district report, finds no attendance change but does find fewer tardies. Which sentence best synthesizes them without overstating either?
options: Source A proves attendance improves, and Source B is simply wrong about the same district
Both sources point to better morning functioning, though they measure it differently: one as attendance, the other as fewer tardies.
Since the sources disagree, neither can be used in the essay
Source B is more reliable because it is a district document, so its null result settles the question
questions.why: Synthesis reconciles two accounts at the level both support rather than picking a winner. Both point to smoother mornings through different measures, which is a real convergence and not a contradiction.

questions.stem: A rocky intertidal community is dominated by mussels until researchers remove the sea star that preys on them. Within a year mussels cover nearly all the rock and species richness falls. Which best explains the outcome?
options: Mussels are a keystone species, and removing their predator increased their competitive dominance
Species richness fell because the sea star had been supplying nutrients the community needed
The sea star was a keystone predator; without it the dominant competitor excludes other species, so diversity falls
Richness fell because the sea star had been a source of disturbance that enriched the habitat
questions.why: The predator is keystone: its effect on diversity is large relative to its abundance because it keeps the dominant competitor below the level where it monopolizes space. Mussels are the dominant competitor, not the keystone species.
